title: Gifts from God
guardrail: God’s gifts are received by grace, not earned. They lead us towards Jesus and service to others, rather than a ranking of faith.
intro: Salvation and life with God are gifts, not rewards for discovering a special ability.
The Spirit’s gifts are given for the common good; believers are called to serve one another.
The Holy Spirit, gifts for service and the fruit of the Spirit are related, but they are not interchangeable lists.
Read the gifts in 1 Corinthians 12 alongside love in chapter 13 and the call to build up the church in chapter 14.
Christians differ about the continuation and practice of some gifts. Start with Scripture in context, prayer and trusted Christian community.
note: These are selected Scripture lists, not one exhaustive total. Some gifts appear in more than one passage. Ministry roles and spiritual fruit are related to gifts for service but are not interchangeable lists. Explanations are original paraphrases; read the linked BSB verse and full chapter.

sections.title: Grace and salvation
sections.summary: Begin with the gifts at the heart of the Gospel.
sections.body: Ephesians presents salvation as God’s gift received through faith. Good works follow grace; they are not the price of being accepted by God. Romans describes eternal life in Christ as God’s gift.

sections.title: The Holy Spirit
sections.summary: Explore the promise and presence of the Spirit.
sections.body: Acts connects repentance and baptism with the promised gift of the Holy Spirit. Ephesians speaks of believers being marked with the promised Spirit. Read the wider passages with your church, recognising differences in how Christians describe receiving, baptism and filling with the Spirit.

sections.title: Gifts for serving
sections.summary: Different gifts, one purpose: building others up in love.

sections.title: Love and the fruit of the Spirit
sections.summary: Understand the character that should shape every gift.
sections.body: Galatians describes the fruit of a life led by the Spirit. Paul’s discussion of gifts in 1 Corinthians is framed by love. Fruit describes character; spiritual gifts concern service. They should not be treated as a scorecard for spiritual worth.

gifts.title: A message of wisdom
gifts.summary: Wisdom shared for the good of the church.
gifts.meaning: Sharing insight that helps people understand and apply God’s wisdom to a situation.
gifts.context: Read 1 Corinthians 12:7–11 together. Different gifts come from the same Spirit and are given for the common good. Wisdom should be considered alongside love and the wider teaching of Scripture.
gifts.example: Someone may help a community consider a difficult question faithfully, bringing clarity while remaining willing to listen and receive correction.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,

gifts.title: A message of knowledge
gifts.summary: Understanding shared to build others up.
gifts.meaning: Sharing understanding that helps others recognise truth and grow in their knowledge of God. Christians differ on precisely how this gift operates.
gifts.context: The knowledge named in 1 Corinthians 12 belongs within the life of the whole body. Read it with chapter 13: knowledge without love does not make a person spiritually superior.
gifts.example: A contribution may help others understand what is true and respond faithfully. Its value is considered through Scripture, love and accountable community.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,

gifts.title: Faith
gifts.summary: Trust in God expressed in service to others.
gifts.meaning: An exceptional confidence in God that strengthens others and supports faithful action in difficult circumstances.
gifts.context: Paul places this gift beside others, distributed by the same Spirit. Read 1 Corinthians 12:9 with verses 7–11 and the description of one body with many members.
gifts.example: A believer may help a community persevere in trust during uncertainty, praying and acting faithfully without promising a particular outcome.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,

gifts.title: Gifts of healing
gifts.summary: God’s healing work, received with hope and care.
gifts.meaning: God bringing healing through believers. Prayer and care remain compassionate, without promising a particular outcome.
gifts.context: The Spirit distributes gifts as he wills, and Paul later asks whether all have gifts of healing. These passages are not grounds for blaming someone whose illness continues. Christians differ about how this gift operates today.
gifts.example: Prayer for someone who is unwell should be accompanied by compassion and practical support. Care for the person matters throughout, including when the outcome is uncertain.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,

gifts.title: Working of miracles
gifts.summary: God’s power at work for his purposes.
gifts.meaning: God acting powerfully through someone in ways beyond ordinary human ability.
gifts.context: Read 1 Corinthians 12:10 within verses 4–11: different gifts, the same God, and the common good. Extraordinary experiences do not remove the need for love, truthfulness and careful discernment. Christian interpretations of present-day practice vary.
gifts.example: A community may give thanks for an extraordinary work while remaining honest about what happened and avoiding claims that exceed the evidence.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

gifts.title: Prophecy
gifts.summary: Speech that strengthens, encourages and comforts.
gifts.meaning: Communicating a message understood to come from God, bringing strengthening, encouragement and comfort. The church is instructed to weigh what is said carefully.
gifts.context: Read 1 Corinthians 12:10 with 14:3 and 14:29. Prophetic speech is to be weighed. Romans 12 also names prophecy. Christians differ about its continuation and relationship to Scripture; the app cannot authenticate a personal message.
gifts.example: A claim to speak prophetically should be considered with Scripture, humility and trusted church leadership, without pressure to accept it unquestioningly.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

gifts.title: Discernment
gifts.summary: Distinguishing between spirits.
gifts.meaning: “Distinguishing between spirits”: evaluating spiritual messages and influences, with careful attention to their source and faithfulness to Christ.
gifts.context: Read 1 Corinthians 12:10 with the common-good purpose in verse 7. First John 4:1–3 separately calls believers to test spirits and attend to their confession of Jesus; that broader instruction supports careful testing without defining every detail of this gift.
gifts.example: When a spiritual claim is made, listen carefully, return to Scripture and consider it with the church. Be ready to revise your judgement rather than treating an impression as certainty.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

gifts.title: Various kinds of tongues
gifts.summary: Spirit-given speech considered with understanding and love.
gifts.meaning: Speaking in languages enabled by the Spirit. Christians differ over whether these always mean recognisable human languages or also include spiritual speech.
gifts.context: Read 1 Corinthians 12:10 alongside chapter 14, especially verses 5 and 27–28. Public use is governed by interpretation and order. Paul’s questions in 12:29–30 also challenge the assumption that everyone has the same gifts.
gifts.example: Questions about this gift are best explored through the connected chapters and trusted church discussion, without making one experience a requirement for spiritual worth.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

gifts.title: Interpretation of tongues
gifts.summary: Making the meaning understandable to the church.
gifts.meaning: Making the meaning of a tongue understandable so that the gathered church can benefit.
gifts.context: Read 1 Corinthians 12:10 with 14:5, 13 and 27–28. These instructions link speech, interpretation and shared understanding. Christian traditions differ about present-day practice, but the concern for the whole congregation is clear.
gifts.example: Where a church practises these gifts, understanding and accountable order matter more than making an experience appear impressive.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

gifts.title: Serving
gifts.summary: Meeting real needs with the strength God supplies.
gifts.meaning: Meeting practical needs through willing, useful action.
gifts.context: Read Romans 12:3–8 for humility and different functions within one body, then 1 Peter 4:10–11. A gift is entrusted for another person’s good; it does not make someone responsible for meeting every need alone.
gifts.example: Preparing a meal, supporting an activity or responding to a practical need can be a faithful way to serve within your circumstances.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;

gifts.title: Teaching
gifts.summary: Helping others understand and respond to Scripture.
gifts.meaning: Explaining Scripture and Christian truth clearly so others can understand and respond faithfully.
gifts.context: Read Romans 12:7 within verses 3–8: humility, belonging and service frame the list. First Corinthians 12:28 also names teachers. A teaching role does not make someone infallible or exempt from correction.
gifts.example: Explain a passage in its context, invite questions and ask trusted believers whether the explanation is faithful, clear and helpful.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;

gifts.title: Encouragement
gifts.summary: Helping others continue in faithful, hopeful response.
gifts.meaning: Strengthening people through comfort, counsel and an appropriate call to faithful action.
gifts.context: Romans 12:8 names this gift; verses 9–13 place community life within sincere love, honour, patience and practical care. Encouragement should make room for lament and another person’s actual circumstances.
gifts.example: Listen first, then offer a truthful word of hope, a relevant Scripture reading or dependable support suited to the person’s need.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.

gifts.title: Giving
gifts.summary: Sharing generously and sincerely for another’s good.
gifts.meaning: Sharing resources generously to meet needs and support others.
gifts.context: Romans 12:8 belongs within a picture of different gifts in one body. Second Corinthians 8:12 separately speaks of a willing gift being acceptable according to what a person has, not what they do not have.
gifts.example: Share resources freely within your means. The size of a gift is not a reliable measure of a person’s faith, and receiving help is not a spiritual failure.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.

gifts.title: Leadership
gifts.summary: Taking responsibility with diligence and care.
gifts.meaning: Taking responsibility for guiding people and their shared work with diligence.
gifts.context: Read Romans 12:8 with verses 3–5, where Paul stresses sober judgement and belonging to one another. Leadership and administration can overlap in practice, but Scripture names them in different lists.
gifts.example: Help a group move towards a shared good, listen to its members, follow through on responsibilities and welcome appropriate accountability.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.

gifts.title: Mercy
gifts.summary: Responding to suffering with compassionate care.
gifts.meaning: Responding to suffering with compassionate, willing care.
gifts.context: Read Romans 12:8 with the chapter’s call to sincere love and to weep with those who weep. Mercy does not require denying pain or assuming hardship reveals a failure of faith.
gifts.example: Be present with someone who is grieving, isolated or struggling. Ask what would help rather than deciding their needs for them.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.

gifts.title: Helping
gifts.summary: Supporting others so the whole community can serve.
gifts.meaning: Supporting others and their work, often through practical assistance that receives little attention.
gifts.context: Read 1 Corinthians 12:28 with verses 21–26: members need one another, and those who appear less prominent are not dispensable. Helping and serving may overlap; these are not competing spiritual ranks.
gifts.example: Support someone carrying a responsibility, offer dependable assistance or make it easier for another person to participate in the life of the church.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.

gifts.title: Administration and guidance
gifts.summary: Helping the community coordinate its shared life.
gifts.meaning: Helping a community organise, coordinate and move wisely towards its shared responsibilities.
gifts.context: Read 1 Corinthians 12:28 alongside the body imagery in the chapter. Coordination should serve people and the common good, rather than making efficiency, status or control an end in itself.
gifts.example: Organise shared work, clarify responsibilities and help people use their contributions well, while remaining attentive to those whose needs could otherwise be overlooked.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.

gifts.title: Apostles
gifts.summary: People commissioned and sent for Christ’s work.
gifts.meaning: People sent to bear witness to Christ and establish the church. Christians differ over how this role applies beyond the original apostles.
gifts.context: Read Ephesians 4:11–16 with 2:19–22. The aim is equipping believers, unity and maturity in Christ. This is a ministry-role passage, not a test that can appoint someone to an office.
gifts.example: Consider how faithful witness and accountable service help the church grow, rather than using a title as a claim to unquestionable personal authority.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers,

gifts.title: Prophets
gifts.summary: People serving through prophetic ministry.
gifts.meaning: People who communicate God’s message, with their words subject to careful discernment.
gifts.context: Read Ephesians 4:11–16 and Paul’s instructions about strengthening others and weighing prophetic speech in 1 Corinthians 14. Christian traditions differ about the continuation and authority of this ministry today.
gifts.example: Assess ministry through its faithfulness to Scripture, service to others and willingness to be accountable, rather than the force of a personal claim.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers,

gifts.title: Evangelists
gifts.summary: People helping others hear the good news of Jesus.
gifts.meaning: People particularly equipped to explain and share the good news of Jesus.
gifts.context: Read Ephesians 4:11 with verses 12–16. This role contributes to shared maturity and service; it does not remove other believers’ calling to bear witness or make persuasion a measure of another person’s worth.
gifts.example: Explain the good news clearly, listen respectfully to questions and help people explore Jesus without pressure or manipulation.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers,

gifts.title: Pastors
gifts.summary: Shepherding people with faithful, accountable care.
gifts.meaning: Shepherds who care for, guide and nurture a Christian community.
gifts.context: Read Ephesians 4:11–16 alongside 1 Peter 5:2–3, which describes willing care and example rather than domineering leadership. Christians organise and understand these ministries in different ways.
gifts.example: Provide patient care, help people engage with Scripture and make room for appropriate support, safeguarding and accountability within the church.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.

namingScripture.text: And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers,

gifts.title: Teachers
gifts.summary: People equipping the church through faithful teaching.
gifts.meaning: People who help the church understand Scripture and mature in faith.
gifts.context: Read Ephesians 4:11–16: teaching serves maturity, steadiness in truth and growth in love. Pastors and teachers are closely connected in the wording, and Christians differ on how the roles are organised.
gifts.example: Help people read Scripture in context, ask honest questions and grow in understanding, while staying open to correction and accountable to the community.
gifts.step: Consider how this reading could shape one act of service. Pray, listen to trusted believers and stay open to correction.
